method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

supports: Routine hand hygiene, task-specific PPE and precautions principles
sourceChecks.scope: Primary guideline retrieved by search; targeted principles, not all-item clinical validation

supports: Disseminated zoster requires airborne and contact precautions
sourceChecks.scope: Targeted precaution cross-check; Canadian sources remain primary for local practice

items.assessment: Changing gloves and hand hygiene before a clean body site is correct, but towel-over-gloves is implausible filler and the key is uniquely complete.
issues: Changing gloves and hand hygiene before a clean body site is correct, but towel-over-gloves is implausible filler and the key is uniquely complete.
proposedChanges: Replace the towel alternative with removing used gloves and applying a fresh pair; explain why hand hygiene is still needed. Keep procedural alternatives similar in length.

items.assessment: Visible soil specifically selects soap and water; the item is honestly labelled foundation and teaches a useful hand-hygiene exception.
Environmental patient-zone contact followed by medication preparation creates a meaningful hand-hygiene transition even without direct touch.
Rubbing until dry is correct and foundation difficulty fits; wiping on clothing is a cartoon shortcut.
issues: Rubbing until dry is correct and foundation difficulty fits; wiping on clothing is a cartoon shortcut.
proposedChanges: Use drying with a clean paper towel as the competing shortcut and explain that premature removal interrupts proper hand-rub application.

items.assessment: Occupational review and compatible skin care are sound, but every alternative is an advertised unsafe abandonment of hygiene or an unapproved product.
issues: Occupational review and compatible skin care are sound, but every alternative is an advertised unsafe abandonment of hygiene or an unapproved product.
proposedChanges: Use plausible competing responses such as switching every encounter to soap and water, adding a second glove layer, or applying a personal moisturizer; explain why compatible product and skin assessment matters.

items.assessment: The barrier tear requires prompt removal and hand hygiene despite no skin injury; covering or disinfecting the damaged glove would leave contamination unaddressed.
Prompt hand hygiene after touching the mask front is correct; wiping and reusing the mask does not meaningfully compete as a response to contaminated fingers.
issues: Prompt hand hygiene after touching the mask front is correct; wiping and reusing the mask does not meaningfully compete as a response to contaminated fingers.
proposedChanges: Use alternatives involving timing of hand hygiene, handling the clean charting device, or gloves. For example, clean the keyboard after charting versus cleaning hands before contact.

items.assessment: The task-specific PPE principle is sound but three generalized good practices compete with one overt only/every barrier strawman.
issues: The task-specific PPE principle is sound but three generalized good practices compete with one overt only/every barrier strawman.
proposedChanges: Make the incorrect alternative a concrete route misconception such as substituting a procedure mask for eye protection when splashing is anticipated. Consider five options and varied correct counts.

items.assessment: A current failed seal check overrides historical fit testing; obtaining suitable protection before the stated airborne-risk entry is defensible.
Required respiratory protection is correct, but holding the breath is implausible and airborne-risk indications could be made specific.
issues: Required respiratory protection is correct, but holding the breath is implausible and airborne-risk indications could be made specific.
proposedChanges: Specify suspected infectious pulmonary TB and replace breath-holding with a credible PPE confusion, such as a face shield plus procedure mask. Keep all actions parallel.

items.assessment: Client source control and receiving-area communication are defensible; borrowing the nurse respirator and abandoning precautions are weak caricatures.
issues: Client source control and receiving-area communication are defensible; borrowing the nurse respirator and abandoning precautions are weak caricatures.
proposedChanges: Use comparable transport plans differing in timing of notification, client masking and route coordination. Shorten the key to match the competing plans.

items.assessment: Known exposure plus compatible symptoms justifies prompt airborne-pathway placement before administrative completion or laboratory confirmation.
Widespread zoster in an immunocompromised client supports airborne plus contact precautions; competing route selections are clinically relevant.
Containing drainage with indicated contact precautions is sound, but a larger linen hamper is unrelated filler and options mix findings with actions.
issues: Containing drainage with indicated contact precautions is sound, but a larger linen hamper is unrelated filler and options mix findings with actions.
proposedChanges: Present four parallel initial actions, such as waiting for culture, standard dressing replacement, containment plus contact measures, or fever-based monitoring. Do not advertise omissions in the alternatives.

items.assessment: A same-shift vomiting/diarrhoea cluster calls for coordinated outbreak response before waiting for cultures or investigating menus alone.
Antibiotic-associated unformed stools justify enteric-pathway precautions, dedicated toileting and clinical assessment while confirmation is pending.
Local IPAC discontinuation criteria are appropriate, but one shower and room preference are implausible clearance criteria.
issues: Local IPAC discontinuation criteria are appropriate, but one shower and room preference are implausible clearance criteria.
proposedChanges: Use plausible but insufficient criteria such as absence of drainage, completion of antibiotics, or a prior admission result; retain organism- and setting-specific review as the key.

items.assessment: Reliable protected care contacts address isolation-associated neglect, but ending precautions and making family provide all care are extreme alternatives.
issues: Reliable protected care contacts address isolation-associated neglect, but ending precautions and making family provide all care are extreme alternatives.
proposedChanges: Compare practical care plans, such as planned toileting contacts, clustering only at medication rounds, extra containment supplies, or repeat call-bell instruction; make the actual access gap decisive.

items.assessment: Observed removal skill is the right outcome; the key is much longer and removing precautions during visits is not a plausible teaching alternative.
issues: Observed removal skill is the right outcome; the key is much longer and removing precautions during visits is not a plausible teaching alternative.
proposedChanges: Compare an illustrated sheet, verbal explanation, teach-back of sequence and observed demonstration. State that the visitor knows the written steps but needs practical removal skill.

items.assessment: Uncontained infectious diarrhoea plus a vulnerable roommate supports early placement review and precautions; curtain or toileting-only changes do not resolve transmission risk.
IPAC compatibility assessment is appropriate, but the available-room alternative advertises its error with before reviewing the infection risks.
issues: IPAC compatibility assessment is appropriate, but the available-room alternative advertises its error with before reviewing the infection risks.
proposedChanges: Use the plain alternative Use the available double room; keep the omitted compatibility assessment in its rationale.

items.assessment: Early source control is correct, but suppressing every cough is cartoon advice.
issues: Early source control is correct, but suppressing every cough is cartoon advice.
proposedChanges: Replace it with a plausible competing task such as arranging a same-day clinical assessment slot; explain why immediate exposure reduction precedes the full visit.

items.assessment: Resolving controls is correct when feasible, but clinical urgency is unspecified and challenge is overstated against obvious PPE substitutes.
issues: Resolving controls is correct when feasible, but clinical urgency is unspecified and challenge is overstated against obvious PPE substitutes.
proposedChanges: State a stable client and nonemergency procedure. Compare feasible locations/timing and protection plans, with appropriately equipped care selected. Avoid implying emergency care must always wait.

items.assessment: Prompt occupational reporting with exposure details permits time-sensitive individualized advice before symptoms; no unsupported fixed exclusion interval is asserted.
Active vomiting creates a food-handling transmission concern even without fever; supervisor notification and local exclusion guidance are appropriate.
